Fresh 1-year daily-return correlation between the two (n=246, get_price_history closes through 2026-09-01) is +0.9928 -- effectively one position split across two tickers, treated as a single combined position for concentration purposes.
items.recommendation: Trim SPYL (the smaller, more redundant leg, 6,240 shares) by roughly a third (~2,080 shares, ~$39,400 at $18.94) and redeploy into DBC (Invesco DB Commodity Index): this run's fresh correlation test found DBC the single best diversifier against the SPY5+SPYL blend (-0.2159) of seven candidates tested (SHY -0.0154, IEF 0.1106, TLT 0.1350, AGG 0.1743, EFA 0.4744, VWO 0.5333). DBC is itself a volatile, inflation-linked asset, not a low-vol ballast -- size it as a genuine diversifier, not a safety cushion (use the SHY ballast below for that).

items.label: Iran-conflict energy-shock tail risk -- limited direct portfolio exposure
items.detail: The Feb 28, 2026 US-Israel military operation against Iran continues to create elevated tail risk for oil markets (Brent scenarios ranging $80-110/bbl per Morgan Stanley and Oxford Economics research, accessed Sept 2, 2026); energy shocks are flagged as both recessionary and inflationary, which would complicate the Fed's September decision. The account holds no pure-play oil & gas exposure -- CCJ is a uranium miner, not oil & gas -- so direct hit is limited, but a broad equity selloff or inflation surprise would still pressure SPY5/SPYL (69.96% of NAV).
items.recommendation: No new position needed given minimal direct energy exposure; the DBC and TLT hedges already recommended above (commodity and duration ballast) would partially cushion an oil-driven inflation or growth shock -- revisit sizing if the conflict visibly escalates or Brent breaks above $100/bbl on a sustained basis.
